title: Toolcall authoring expressions and failure-mode protocol
creator: Avery Chen
description: Define a compact, expressive JSON schema authoring format for tool/function calls that supports computed defaults (authoring expressions), explicit compatibility hints, and a failure-mode protocol for human-friendly errors and automated recovery. Deliver a runtime validator, a compatibility adaptor layer, and a canonical error taxonomy with remediation advice and telemetry hooks.
background: We currently have ad-hoc JSON param shapes across SDKs and runtimes. Engineering and SDK consumers ask for: 1) a way to declare derived/default values so authors don't repeat prompt-side logic; 2) a compatibility story when consumers call older call manifests; 3) consistent error messages that are actionable for integrators. Past tickets focused on validation and coercion, but none capture an authoring expression model or a structured failure-mode protocol.
proposal: Introduce a 'call manifest v1-expr' format with three orthogonal extensions: 1) authoring expressions — a minimal expression grammar for computed defaults and simple conditional validation; 2) compatibility metadata — fields for 'introduced_in', 'deprecated_in', and 'compatibility_level' (strict|lenient|adapter); 3) failure-mode protocol — canonical error codes plus 'remediation' strings that UIs/SDKs can surface. Implement a runtime adaptor that can apply backwards-compatible coercions (e.g., string->int with hinting) and emits standardized telemetry events. Provide a Python/TS reference validator and a CLI linter for authors.
decision_log:
2026-03-05: PM and Eng alignment: move forward with expression subset (no Turing-complete features) and require opt-in for compatibility_adaptor.
2026-03-08: Design review: error messages must contain 'short_code' and 'user_hint'. Keep coercion rules explicit; do not perform silent lossy coercion without 'coercion:explicit'.
acceptance_criteria: Specification: a one-page grammar for authoring expressions and examples for computed defaults
Validator: reference implementation (Python) that accepts v1-expr manifests and rejects unsupported constructs
Adaptor: compatibility adaptor that can upgrade v0->v1 manifests for at least two back-compat cases (missing nested object, short->long enum)
Errors: canonical error taxonomy with at least 12 codes and example remediations
Docs: docs/guide and SDK examples (JS + Python) showing error handling and telemetry events
implementation_steps: Reference validator: initial pass (Maya) - Python package with unit tests
Compatibility adaptor: implement two adapters and integration tests (Maya + Eng interns)
Error taxonomy: PM-led workshop to finalize codes and remediations (includes UX examples)
SDK integrations: add error mapping helpers in node and python SDKs
Linter: CLI rule to flag non-authoring-expression-safe constructs
Rollout: opt-in feature flag for hosted API; enable logging/telemetry keys
telemetry_and_errors: Error codes (examples): INVALID_TYPE | MISSING_REQUIRED | COERCION_APPLIED | EXPR_EVAL_ERROR | INCOMPATIBLE_MANIFEST
Each error must include: short_code, human_message, remediation_hint, telemetry_key
Telemetry should capture: manifest_id, manifest_version, sdk_version, adaptor_applied (bool), latency_ms
docs_and_links: Related tickets: ENG-999999 (call-shape spec), ENG-962345 (runtime telemetry)
risks: Expression complexity creep: authors might try to encode heavy logic into manifests; mitigation: explicit lint rules and runtime limits
Silent coercions causing subtle bugs: mitigation: require explicit flags and emit COERCION_APPLIED telemetry
Backward compatibility gaps across SDKs: mitigation: implement adaptor and test matrix across 3 SDK versions
blockers: Sign-off on error taxonomy from Product and Design
Access to existing manifest corpus for empirical compatibility cases (data team)
Runtime turf: need alignment with Serving runtime team on where validation occurs (edge vs control plane)
notes: Authoring expression subset proposal: arithmetic, string templates, simple path lookups (no loops, no external IO). Example: default: "{{user.country == 'US' ? 'zipcode' : 'postal_code'}}"
Compatibility examples: when 'introduced_in' missing, assume 0. When 'compatibility_level' == 'adapter', runtime may rewrite calls according to adapter ruleset
Error UX: SDKs should map short_code -> localized human_message, and expose remediation_hint as actionable button (e.g., 'Convert field to integer')
